verdict.root_cause: A platform-automation traffic-shaping container was attached to cartservice's network namespace at 08:29:32, imposing a fixed 300ms zero-jitter egress delay on eth0 with no removal recorded, unlike the three earlier self-resolving iterations of the same automated cycle [tr_0e856a4a6361]. Every packet leaving the cart pod pays 300ms, which appears in traces as a hard ~300ms floor on cartservice's Redis leaf spans (HGET/HMSET, nearly all self-time) while the cartservice handler itself contributes under 2ms, plus a duplicated ~300ms on caller-side client spans in frontend and checkoutservice [tr_302ff7824a9d]. The delay is additive per cart operation, inflating checkout roots to ~2.45-2.49s while non-cart dependencies stay in single-digit ms [tr_302ff7824a9d], which pushes checkoutservice calls past deadlines and produces its bursty ~17% error ratio against a ~0.2% baseline [tr_39eb73a5217c]. cartservice itself serves normally with no error text [tr_fbb6346f0941]. The mechanism is waiting on an artificially slowed call path; removing the injected shaper stops it.
verdict.reasoning: The change record places a 300ms fixed-delay shaper on cartservice's network namespace three minutes before onset, still in effect [tr_0e856a4a6361]. Traces measure exactly that quantum, and the two-sided signature - delay on cart-to-Redis requests and again on cart-to-caller responses - is what egress shaping on the cart pod predicts and what a genuinely slow Redis cannot produce, since a slow Redis could not add 300ms to a frontend client span that already wholly contains the cartservice server span [tr_302ff7824a9d]. Callers' symptoms follow from cart: checkout errors are deadline exhaustion while cart logs show only successful operations through 08:35:05 [tr_fbb6346f0941, tr_39eb73a5217c]. The competing config and image candidates were both reverted before onset [tr_0e856a4a6361].
open_questions: checkoutservice's only error-ratio change point is 08:10:45, ~19 minutes before the shaper was attached [tr_39eb73a5217c]; that earlier degradation coincides with the hotfix.2 image window and is not explained by shaping, so the incident may have two phases.
No cartservice CPU, memory, request-rate or restart data exists - its metric series is empty in both incident and baseline windows [tr_18f1d86128f2].

Neither traces nor logs cover 08:32:45 itself (traces start 08:34:01; log truncation dropped the middle) [tr_302ff7824a9d, tr_fbb6346f0941], so onset timing is inferred from the untrusted change record.

alternatives.root_cause: The cartservice hotfix.2 image caused the 08:10:45 error onset and remains the true fault, with shaping only a later overlay.
alternatives.why_not: The image reference was reverted ~13 minutes before onset and the baseline image was running at onset [tr_0e856a4a6361]; it cannot explain the ~300ms floor measured after 08:34.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart became slow, and cartservice failed because it waited on its cache.
alternatives.why_not: A slow Redis cannot add a second ~300ms to caller client spans that already enclose the full cartservice server span [tr_302ff7824a9d], and a documented egress shaper explains both increments [tr_0e856a4a6361].

proposal.expected_effect: Removing the injected 300ms/0-jitter eth0 shaper should drop cartservice's Redis leaf spans (HGET/HMSET) from ~300ms self-time to single-digit ms, remove the duplicated ~300ms on frontend and checkoutservice client spans, and bring checkout roots down from ~2.45-2.49s. checkoutservice error ratio should decay from ~0.17 toward its ~0.0025 baseline. Judge cartservice via traces and logs, not its error-ratio series, which is empty in both windows.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if fresh traces after 10 minutes still show a ~300ms floor on HGET/HMSET with sub-2ms handler self-time - then the shaper is outside what revert_config restores, or the platform automation re-attached it, and the fix is to stop that automation. Expected partial miss: checkoutservice errors may persist, since its only change point is 08:10:45, ~19 min before the attach and inside the hotfix.2 window.
proposal.risk: Recreates the container, so a brief cart outage for no gain if wrong, and it destroys the live shaper as forensic evidence. If 'previous configuration' resolves to a stale generation, it could reintroduce the reverted REDIS_ADDR:6380 endpoint and turn a latency fault into a hard cart failure. In-flight cart calls are dropped.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice's inbound callers: frontend and checkoutservice see connection resets during the recreate, and loadgenerator sees the resulting checkout errors. Redis-cart sees a short traffic pause then a return to full-rate cart operations.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerted within 15s starting at cartservice and propagating up through checkoutservice and frontend to the load generator, which is a user-visible failure path rather than a single quiet warning. The cartservice-first ordering suggests a downstream dependency or its backing store degrading, but that is only a prior for dispatch ordering.
